Spent the last 2 Saturdays redoing the electric in a buddy's shed. I've been doing this 26 years and I still came home both days going "how is that place still standing." So here's the list of what we found, because it was honestly hilarious, and then I'm gonna get serious for a minute so stick with me.

1. Power to the shed was 3 orange extension cords daisy chained together. Out the basement window, across the whole yard, and under the deck. Permanent. Like that's just how the shed gets power now.

2. One of the splices between cords was wrapped in DUCT tape. Not electrical tape. Duct tape. The gray stuff. I stood there looking at it for a solid minute.

3. 30 amp breaker feeding 14 gauge wire. For the non electricians, that means the wire gives up and catches fire way before the breaker ever thinks about tripping. The breaker's just sitting there watching it happen.

4. The outlet in the shed was hooked up with speaker wire. Speaker wire. Somebody had a Bose and a dream.

5. The "GFCI" was a regular outlet with a GFCI sticker slapped on it. Didn't know they made those stickers. Kind of impressed honestly.

6. Ceiling fan box was held up by ONE drywall screw. One. That fan was spinning over people's heads hanging on by its fingernails.

7. Mouse nest inside the junction box. Mice were fine. Totally unbothered. They had heat, they had a roof, they're doing better than some of us.

8. And my favorite. I open the panel and on the inside of the door in sharpie it says "SHED - DONT TOUCH - RON." My wife is standing right behind me and goes "who's Ron?" Like I'd know. Nobody knows who Ron is. Ron's gone. But Ron left us a message and we did not listen.

What we did: trenched it 18 inches, ran 12/2 UF, put in a 20 amp GFCI breaker, real box, real outlets (with real GFCI protection, no sticker), and the fan's on a proper brace now. Got paid in 2 pizzas and a case of Yuengling, which is the correct rate for family and friends.

Ok now the serious part.

Every single thing on that list is a fire. Not "might be a problem someday." Wrong breaker on that wire size, a splice sitting out in the rain under duct tape, a fake GFCI out in a shed where you're standing on concrete with wet boots, that's how houses burn down and that's how people get hurt. And the whole time it looked like it was "working." Lights came on. Fan spun. That's the scary part, it works right up until it doesn't.

And I want to be fair to Ron. I don't think Ron was a bad guy. I think Ron was cheap and a little proud and figured he could handle it, and that's like 90% of what I find out there. Nobody's trying to burn their house down. They just didn't want to pay somebody, or they had a buddy who "knows electric," or they watched a couple videos and figured how hard can it be.

So please. If you need an outlet put in, a circuit run to the garage, power out to a shed, anything like that, call a licensed electrician. Not your buddy. Not your nephew's friend who watched a bunch of YouTube videos and will do it for cash this weekend. A licensed guy who pulls a permit and gets it inspected. Yeah it costs more up front. It costs a lot less than a fire, and your homeowners insurance is gonna have some questions if they find speaker wire in the wall.

The videos aren't the problem. Some of them are fine. The problem is the video doesn't know what's in YOUR panel, what size YOUR wire is, or what Ron did 15 years ago that nobody wrote down except "dont touch."

If you're not sure who to call, message me and I'll point you to somebody good. That's free, no pizza required. (Yuengling still accepted.)

Pics below. Look at that duct tape and tell me I'm wrong.
